subject: SLA addendum request: burst protection and order-form language
messages:
From: Ellen Wright <ellen.wright@alphamed.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@alphamed.com
Date: 2026-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA addendum: burst traffic protection & credits

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Quick context: AlphaMed sees a predictable pattern of short, high-volume bursts (30–60 minutes) tied to batch jobs and nightly patient record synchronizations. Those bursts push our usage above the standard 95th percentile assumptions used in your default SLA and cause us concern about operational exposure and billing unpredictability.

We'd like to request an addendum to the MSA/order form that:
- Defines a "burst protection" carve-out (for example: allowable monthly burst volume up to X% without penalty, or a credit schedule for burst-induced failures).
- Provides clear evidence items you will accept to validate burst incidents (service logs, per-route token counts, KV cache hit rates).
- Specifies an emergency mitigation path (temporary burst buffer or prioritized queueing) and an escalation contact.

Could you share proposed order-form language and the evidence checklist you would accept for disputes? I attached a short sample of our traffic (alpha-slo-traffic-sample.csv) so you can see the shape.

Thanks,
Ellen Wright
Director, Cloud Ops
AlphaMed Systems

(attachment: alpha-slo-traffic-sample.csv)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Wright <ellen.wright@alphamed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum: burst traffic protection & credits

Ellen — thanks for the clear note and the sample. This is a reasonable ask and something we've seen before for customers with bursty ETL/workload patterns.

Two pragmatic paths we typically propose:
1) Burst forgiveness window — an amount of monthly burst traffic (percent of peak or absolute token threshold) treated as excluded from uptime calculations; OR
2) Credits + mitigation — a defined credit schedule when burst-related degradation occurs plus a temporary mitigation (e.g., short-term reserved burst capacity) that we can enable on request.

I'll loop in Karthik and Neha to draft order-form wording and an evidence checklist. I've attached an internal draft (redwood-burst-proposal-v1.pdf) with the high-level options so we have something to iterate on.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik: can you sketch the technical limits and what metrics we can provide as evidence?
- Neha: can you outline procurement/legal guardrails (credit tables, caps, timing)?
- Emily/Monica: if we need an ops-runbook or on-call escalation, can Monica propose an SLA contact flow?

Happy to set a short call if that helps.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

(attachment: redwood-burst-proposal-v1.pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Wright <ellen.wright@alphamed.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T08:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum: burst traffic protection & credits

Ellen / team — quick technical notes from infra/runtime perspective:
- We can surface per-route token throughput and per-request latency histograms for any customer. Those are good evidence items.
- For short bursts, prefix/KV caching and auto-batching reduce load significantly if the traffic shape is similar; we'll include hit-rate metrics.
- Mitigation options we can practically offer: short-term reserved burst pool (30–120 minutes), prioritized routing to dedicated capacity (if customer has Dedicated contract), or autoscale pre-warm.

Draft order-form clause suggestion (for discussion):
"""
Burst Protection Addendum:
Redwood will exclude from Availability calculations any customer usage classified as "Burst Traffic" up to 10% of the customer's monthly peak token volume, provided that the customer supplies the traffic sample and related logs within 7 days of an incident. For incidents exceeding this threshold, Availability credits will be applied according to the Credit Schedule in Appendix A. Bursts must be validated by Redwood using mutually agreed evidence (per-route token counts, request-level latency histograms, and KV cache hit metrics).
"""
I'll attach a quick plain-text snippet (draft-clause-burst-protection.txt) for legal to iterate on.

-Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

(attachment: draft-clause-burst-protection.txt)

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ellen Wright <ellen.wright@alphamed.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-17T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum: burst traffic protection & credits

Team — procurement/finance lens:
- We prefer explicit crediting rules vs open carve-outs to avoid ambiguity in renewals. Proposed credit table:
  - Availability < 99.9% for the month (excluding validated burst allowance): 5% credit of monthly committed fees
  - Availability < 99.5%: 10% credit
  - Availability < 99.0%: 20% credit
- Cap total credits to 50% of monthly fees.
- Evidence list to accept disputes: per-route token logs, 10-second latency percentiles, KV cache hit-rate, and a signed incident runbook entry from customer side.
- Timing: customer must submit incident evidence within 14 days; Redwood will respond with validation within 7 business days.

Attaching procurement template for SLA amendments so legal can reference common order-form fields.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Manager, Contracts & Procurement, Redwood Inference

(attachment: procurement-template-sla-amendment.docx)

From: Ellen Wright <ellen.wright@alphamed.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-18T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum: burst traffic protection & credits

Thanks — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifications from AlphaMed:
- We'd like an ability to request "emergency burst mitigation" that Redwood can enable for up to 2 hours while we address our ingestion pipeline; this should include an on-call contact with a guaranteed 15-minute acknowledgment window.
- DocuSign flow: we'll need the addendum attached to the existing MSA (deal AM-2026-478). Can you send a signing link once you have final language?

Assuming the credit table you suggested is acceptable, we're happy to proceed. Please include the escalation contact (name, role, phone, email) in the addendum.

Best,
Ellen

(attachment: signature-request-docusign.pdf)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Wright <ellen.wright@alphamed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-20T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA addendum: burst traffic protection & credits

Ellen — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is the final addendum draft (final-sla-addendum-v1.pdf) with the agreed credit table, the burst allowance language (10% monthly peak by default), and the emergency mitigation clause. Key points summarized below: 

- Burst Allowance: up to 10% of monthly peak token volume excluded from Availability calculations when validated per evidence checklist.
- Credit Schedule: as proposed by Neha, cap at 50% of monthly fees.
- Emergency Burst Mitigation: Redwood will enable a temporary burst pool on request for up to 2 hours with a guaranteed 15-minute acknowledgment from our on-call team. Escalation contact: Monica Patel, Sr. Customer Reliability Manager, +1-415-555-0198, monica.patel@redwood.com.
- Evidence & Timing: Customer must submit evidence within 14 days; Redwood validates within 7 business days.

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-def456 (this link will attach the addendum to MSA AM-2026-478).

If this matches AlphaMed's expectations, please sign and we'll countersign the same day.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this wrapped up quickly.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

(attachment: final-sla-addendum-v1.pdf)
